_provenance.description: New cross-framework arms for the two discrete-latent PPLBench models under the STANDARD protocol, filling the missing cells of the four-framework comparison figure: (1) crowd_sourced_annotation gains a Turing.jl arm; (2) noisy_or_topic gains NumPyro and Turing.jl arms. Reference (existing) rows quoted in this file are reused verbatim from annotation_numpyro_results_2026-07-10.json and g4_results_G4_2026-07-06_052754.json and were NOT re-run.
_provenance.protocol: PPLBench trials-as-chains: 4 trials, iterations=4000, num_warmup=1000, single chain per trial, shared trial seeds derived from model seed 12345; overall n_eff = arviz.ess over all params with the 4 trials as 4 chains; n_eff/s = overall n_eff / mean steady-state inference wall time (trials 1..3, excluding the compile trial 0); PLL = per-trial final cumulative predictive log-likelihood on the held-out test split. All runs CPU (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""), --threads 32, NUTS step_size=0.1, max_tree_depth=10, adapt_step_size, adapt_mass_matrix (Turing NUTS(n_adapts, 0.8; DenseEuclideanMetric), same harness settings as the other standard-model Turing runs; NumPyro NUTS dense_mass=True via numpyro_harness.py).
deviations: The first Turing noisy_or_topic attempt was killed externally after trial 1 (a 1-hour background-task limit in the driving harness, not a benchmark failure). The arm was re-run to completion; the re-run reproduced the killed attempt's per-trial results (trial 0: 1089.46s vs 1105.52s, trial 1: 956.65s vs 957.91s; PLLs bit-identical at -28.5420 / -28.4018), confirming determinism of the seeded runs.

Turing crowd trial 3 landed in the known label-permutation mode (PLL -1853.32). The same mode appears in the reference arms under the shared trial seeds (NumPyro trial 3: -1849.52; Stan trial 2: -1847.41) and is documented in annotation_numpyro_results_2026-07-10.json; it also explains the low cross-chain min/median ESS (~7-8) seen identically in the NumPyro and Stan reference arms.

model_math.crowd_sourced_annotation: Marginalized Dawid-Skene (ACL Q14-1025). Continuous latents: prev (K-simplex prevalence, Dirichlet(1/K)) and confusion_matrix (k*K independent K-simplices; row for true category c ~ Dirichlet(alpha[c]), alpha[c] = concentration * [expected_correctness on the diagonal, (1-expected_correctness)/(K-1) off-diagonal]). The discrete per-item true label is marginalized analytically: per item i, target += logsumexp_c( sum_j log conf[labeler_ij, c, label_ij] + log prev[c] ). The new Turing.jl model (turing/standard/crowd_sourced_annotation.jl) implements exactly this density: the k*K Dirichlet simplices are one matrix-variate arraydist (column (c-1)*k+l = obs-label simplex of labeler l under true category c) and the per-item logsumexp is vectorized via a precomputed column-major gather index over all 1000 train items, so Turing's NUTS targets the IDENTICAL continuous posterior as the Stan, NumPyro and Impulse reference arms. n=2000 -> 1000 train / 1000 test items, k=10 annotators, 3 categories, seed 12345.
model_math.noisy_or_topic: Noisy-Or Topic (LAKI) boolean Bayesian network: always-on leak node, 50 topic nodes, 100 word nodes, edge_weight fixed data. The discrete topic vector `active` cannot be sampled by a continuous-only NUTS PPL, so all continuous arms (Stan upstream, Impulse, and the two new arms) use the SAME Gumbel-softmax continuous relaxation at temperature tau=0.1: two Gumbel(0,1) latent vectors g_true/g_false of length 1+num_topics; per topic j in topological order aw_j = edge_weight[j,:j] . active_true[:j], active_true[j] = sigmoid(((log1m_exp(-aw_j)+aw_j) + (g_true[j]-g_false[j]))/tau) (the softmax 'true' coordinate; leak pinned to 1); word logits S_logit = log1m_exp(-S_weight) + S_weight with S_weight = edge_weight[words,:] . active_true, S ~ Bernoulli(logits=S_logit) on the single training sentence. The posterior over (g_true, g_false) is therefore IDENTICAL to the Stan/Impulse relaxation posterior (an APPROXIMATE relaxation of the discrete model, not an exact marginalization). The boolean `active` is recovered post hoc by argmax over the 2-way relaxation (lt > lf, tau-invariant) in the extract step, exactly like the Stan extract's argmax over the size-2 axis. The new NumPyro arm (ppls/numpyro/noisy_or_topic.py) writes the recursion as a plain Python loop over the 51 static topics under JIT; the new Turing arm (turing/standard/noisy_or_topic.jl) writes it as the same sequential Julia loop. num_topics=50, num_words=100, n=2 -> 1 train / 1 test sentence, seed 12345.
